derivation_notes.gstr1.tax_export: Exports are always inter-static: iamt = round(txval * rt * 0.01, 2), and there is no central/state branch at all. An export WITHOUT payment of tax (WOPAY) zeroes both the integrated tax and the cess, whatever the rate says. csamt = round(Cess Amount, 2) otherwise, or 0 when blank.

notes.text: Line items here are BARE: no `num` and no `itm_det` wrapper, so the rate, taxable value and tax sit directly on the item object. Only the amended B2C(Small) section shares that shape, and it has no iamt.

The payload groups by EXPORT TYPE, not by counterparty or place of supply — one envelope for WPAY and one for WOPAY, each holding its invoices. There is no recipient at all: exports are to persons outside India.

An export WITHOUT payment of tax (WOPAY) zeroes both the integrated tax and the cess regardless of the rate entered, the same way SEZ-without-payment does in the B2B sections. The rate itself is still required and still emitted.

Shipping bill details are all-or-nothing but the pair as a whole is OPTIONAL: an exporter may file before the shipping bill exists and supply it in a later amendment. The reference switches between two validation branches on whether either field is present.
Port Code is optional and, unusually, permits any alphanumeric string of up to six characters — it is not checked against a list of real ports.

The template has no 'Applicable % of Tax Rate' column, yet the reference's validation writes a default of 100 into the row before mapping it, which makes the key exist and sets diff_percent to 1. Since only 0.65 survives into the upload file, the effect is invisible — no such key is ever emitted. No field is declared here for that reason.

Shipping Bill Number is digits only, three to seven of them, so it is emitted as a string but constrained like a number. The reference compares it both as a string and via parseInt when matching rows, which papers over any leading-zero difference.

The reference groups rows into one amendment when EITHER the revised or the original invoice number matches, then rejects the group on any other disagreement. Grouping here keys on the revised number alone. Same unresolved question as the other amendment sections.

Nothing requires the revised invoice to postdate the original, nor the shipping bill date to follow the invoice date — the routine that looks like it enforces the latter returns before checking anything.

Cess Amount is not validated at all in this section — the reference's field checks for exports cover the export type, invoice details, port, shipping bill, rate and taxable value, but never the cess. A negative cess is therefore accepted and reaches the payload as a negative csamt. This implementation applies the unsigned amount pattern instead, since a negative cess on an export is not a thing the portal should be asked to accept. Confirmed by differential test against the tool.
